A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELLSA/SA-MoE work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-interaction, simulated robot-manipulation, full-duplex, and context-grounded VQA results, together with dense-model and individual-expert comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds model ablations, inference-latency measurements, and CALVIN experiments in Appendices G and H.

M1.justification: The principal two-expert SA-MoE architecture and three-stage training procedure are retained. Appendix G introduces bounded model variants: a SPEAR/Zipformer speech encoder and three-expert configurations separating vision from action or speech from text.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds CALVIN's simulated environments and five-task manipulation sequences to the retained LIBERO and speech-task coverage. This extends coverage within simulated robot manipulation; the other new ablations reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets are retained. The new CALVIN comparison in Table 12 substantially expands evaluated comparators with MCIL, RT-1, Robo-Flamingo, GR-1, UP-VLA, and RoboVLMs. Its speech comparison retains Moshi and Freeze-Omni.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental settings through block-duration, expert-count, and encoder comparisons plus A100 per-block latency measurements. The 0.48-second variant generates four text tokens and five action frames per block. CALVIN introduces ABCD-to-D training/testing, five-task chains terminating at failure, and chain-success and average-length metrics. These are added protocols; the original protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's dense-model and individual-expert comparisons, Appendix G adds three substantive ablation studies. They test the accuracy/latency tradeoff of shorter blocks, two versus three experts, and whether a stronger speech encoder reduces degradation during speaking-while-acting.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Existing evaluation episode counts are retained; the new tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original result values are retained, while Tables 9-12 add substantial results for new configurations and CALVIN. Examples include speech-to-speech latency of 854 versus 455 ms for 1-second versus 0.48-second blocks, SPEAR concurrent LIBERO LONG success of 86.2% versus Mamba's 73.2%, and CALVIN average chain length of 4.43 for ELLSA versus 4.49 for RoboVLMs. These are configuration or benchmark comparisons, not revisions of unchanged-setting v1 scores.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The new material consists of empirical experiments and their interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same SA-MoE contribution, full-duplex multimodal novelty claim, advanced interaction capabilities, and competitive-performance claims. Replacing several AGI references with human-like intelligence changes framing without redefining the claimed capabilities.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds explanations linking shorter action sequences to reduced temporal coherence, favoring two experts for efficiency, and attributing concurrent-task degradation primarily to model capacity following the SPEAR experiment. Appendix H interprets CALVIN results as supporting adaptation through task-specific experts. The original limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents token/action counts for the shorter-block variant, initialization of separated experts, the SPEAR encoder, and hardware for latency measurements. The abstract also supplies a repository destination for promised code, data, and checkpoints. Release remains prospective; the PDFs do not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds Gato, PaLM-E, and an explicit comparison with Unified-IO 2. Appendix F adds EVEv2 and Mono-InternVL citations, while new experiments introduce CALVIN, SPEAR, and comparator references. These are localized extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact. v2 makes localized terminology edits and inserts Appendices G and H, shifting the former G-I to I-K. It also introduces incorrect cross-references: Section 5.1.1 points to Table 12 instead of Table 1, and G.2 points to Table 11 instead of Table 10.

P2.justification: New multipart Tables 9-12 substantially expand the displayed evidence with block-duration/latency comparisons, expert-count ablations, independent-versus-concurrent encoder results, and CALVIN chain-success results. Figures 1-8 and existing table content are retained; main-text tables shift position, and former Tables 9-11 become Tables 13-15.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in support for ELLSA's design and real-time feasibility. Table 9 supplies measured inference times within both block budgets; Tables 10-11 test architectural choices and concurrent-task degradation; Table 12 extends validation beyond LIBERO. These additions materially strengthen the empirical foundation of the central claims while preserving the original evidence. Incorrect cross-references and an overstrong capacity-versus-architecture causal interpretation reduce clarity and rigor, but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
